settings.heading:
Bodology:
The Studies
settings.subtext: Transparency comes first. Here is the research behind what we make, laid out study by study.

settings.label: Placebo-controlled
settings.popup_text: A "placebo-controlled" study is one in which one group receives the actual product while another receives an inactive look-alike, or placebo. This method allows researchers to distinguish the product's physical effects from the psychological impact of a participant's belief that the product is working.

settings.label: Double-blind
settings.popup_text: "Double-blind" means that in a clinical study, neither participants nor researchers know who receives which product, preventing bias and ensuring objective results.

settings.label: Randomized
settings.popup_text: Part of a gold-standard study, "randomization" means assigning participants to groups (experimental or placebo) based on chance to compare outcome results fairly and minimize bias.
